hypothesis: PDL progenitor-seeded, root-topography-guided reconstruction can restore a functional cementum–PDL–bone attachment.
evidence_basis: Rat replantation study reports PDL-like tissue, fiber insertion, near-control force-induced displacement, and 22/22 firm attachment after treatment.
key_unknown: Cell source, manufacturing, immune context, safety, periodontal disease background, and whether an intact in-situ tooth can be repaired without extraction.
decisive_next_experiment: Compare cell-seeded and cell-free root-mimetic interfaces under matched cyclic load; measure both-interface insertion, mobility, toughness, ankylosis, root resorption, pulp viability and durability after temporary support removal.
falsifier: Near-control stiffness with absent fiber insertion, excessive bridging, poor mobility/toughness, loss of vitality, or relapse after support removal.
translation_to_in_situ_trauma: Promising attachment proof-of-concept only; no evidence yet it can reposition a crooked in-situ tooth or eliminate all temporary stabilization.

hypothesis: Local signaling that supports PDL fibroblast repair while suppressing osteogenic bridging can improve restoration quality.
evidence_basis: Rat tooth-replantation PDGF-BB study reports reduced ankylosis, organized fibers and improved mechanical outcomes, but day-21 failure load and toughness remain below control.
key_unknown: Dose and exposure window, reproducibility, human relevance, pulpal effects, long-term loading and whether area-normalized strength ratio is 72.3% or the paper's stated approximately 76%.
decisive_next_experiment: Repeat with prespecified mechanical and histologic endpoints, per-tooth source data, pulp/vascular assessment, blinded scoring and follow-up after loading.
falsifier: Improved stiffness without restored toughness/mobility, persistent pulpal injury, or unchanged ankylosis/resorption.
translation_to_in_situ_trauma: Potential modifier of local healing environment; does not itself specify positional correction or prove no retention is needed.

hypothesis: A cell-free, spatially instructive interface may recruit host progenitors while preserving fiber orientation and mineralization boundaries.
evidence_basis: Root microtopography studies show progenitor adhesion/signaling and in-vivo reconstruction; cell-free replant controls in the same study performed poorly.
key_unknown: Whether topographic/material cues alone can recruit enough appropriate host cells and form both insertions in a damaged, perfused human socket.
decisive_next_experiment: Factorial study varying surface chemistry/topography, scaffold degradation and host-cell access with matched progenitor-seeded positive controls.
falsifier: No oriented fibers, absent insertion at either boundary, poor force recovery, or bridge formation across the ligament space.
translation_to_in_situ_trauma: Could reduce cell-manufacturing burden, but currently weaker direct evidence than cell-seeded reconstruction.

hypothesis: Regenerative attachment plus a defined temporary position-restoration phase could permit durable alignment without lifelong external retention.
evidence_basis: No direct human evidence in the reviewed sources; this is the user's stated engineering requirement.
key_unknown: Original tooth position, trauma severity, alveolar geometry, remodeling and relapse after device removal.
decisive_next_experiment: Longitudinal model that declares a pre-injury position target, measures tooth/socket geometry and attachment, then removes temporary support and tracks position under physiological load.
falsifier: Persistent drift, healing at an unintended position, or stable alignment only while support remains.
translation_to_in_situ_trauma: The decisive question is unsupported positional stability after native tissue function returns; the current evidence does not answer it.
